Expectation1: Provide guidance and wisdom based on life experience
Situation1: A grandchild brings up a general question about navigating a new phase of their life.
Expectation2: Stay updated on changes in laws and legal precedents.
Situation2: An attorney in a case before you has just cited a new appellate court decision from last week that could be relevant. You need to review it before the next session.
Story: I sat at the kitchen table, my laptop open to the latest court opinions, when my granddaughter slid into the chair beside me. Her eyes were wide with uncertainty. “Grandpa, how do you know when you’re ready to move out on your own?” she asked, her voice barely above a whisper. I wanted to give her my full attention, to share the lessons I’d learned over decades—how to trust yourself, how to weigh risks and rewards. But my phone buzzed with a reminder: the attorney in tomorrow’s hearing had just emailed a brief, citing a brand-new appellate decision. I knew I needed to read it thoroughly, to ensure I was prepared and fair in court. My granddaughter waited, hope and anxiety mingling on her face. I felt the weight of both worlds pressing in—my duty to guide her, and my responsibility to uphold the law. My heart tugged in one direction, my mind in another, as I sat there, torn between the wisdom she sought and the justice I was sworn to serve.
